name: Explorer pony
tips: RTFM means "Read The F*** Manual": before asking, look in the docs. The answer is often already written there.
A project's docs start with its README, then its doc/ folder. Installed programs keep theirs in /usr/share/doc.
When you ask for help, say which docs you read: people help faster, and nobody needs to answer RTFM.
`git clone` copies a whole project to your computer, history included, so you can read every file.
`ls -a` shows hidden files too: their names start with a dot, and they often hold settings.
`tree -L 2` draws a folder and its subfolders, two levels deep: a quick map of a new project.
personal: You went through the repo! Real explorers read the code.
Every folder is a new trail.
I always say what I see: that file needs a README.
